correspondences.rationale: Both denote a hard transmitter-laser failure that removes the optical channel at the remote receiver.
Both denote a hard card-level failure that interrupts traffic and monitoring and may mask consequent traffic alarms.
Both denote a receiver-local degradation causing pre-FEC errors while the path and other channels remain normal.
Both denote a physical fibre discontinuity that prevents optical propagation.
Both denote failure of the current or preceding amplifier such that no usable light is emitted.
Both denote an open optical connection caused by a removed jumper or patch cord.
Both denote a ROADM port state or fault that blocks onward passage of a channel.
Both denote abnormally increased fibre attenuation that reduces delivered power and margin.
Both denote excess amplifier noise that lowers OSNR while optical signal power may remain present.
Both denote increased differential group delay along the optical path.
Both denote spectral misalignment of a WSS passband that impairs one channel despite potentially normal power.
Both denote a polarization change too fast for coherent-receiver tracking.
Both denote connector contamination introducing loss or reflection and degrading signal quality.
Both are generic failure causes used when the particular defect class is unspecified.
Both denote an amplifier gain deficiency relative to target, causing weak output and OSNR penalty.
Both denote incipient pump deterioration requiring increasing drive current and eventually raising an end-of-life alarm.
Both denote wavelength-dependent gain imbalance that weakens channels near a band edge.
Both denote hard failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric that disrupts services and propagates ODU-AIS.
Both denote an ODU provisioning or switching error that routes an ODU to the wrong destination without an optical symptom.
Both denote hard failure of a client-facing port at either endpoint, interrupting the service.
Both denote gradual WSS attenuation increase above the configured value for one channel.
Both denote hard failure of one WSS input that blocks all channels from that ingress while other inputs remain unaffected.
Both denote absence of detectable optical light at the line receiver.
Both denote inability to recover OTU framing, including cases where light remains present.
Both denote a detected internal card hardware defect causing equipment alarm and consequent traffic effects.
Both denote suppression of derivative traffic alarms by the primary equipment alarm.
Both are the same composite optical/receiver degradation class covering low power, poor OSNR, DGD, filtering, receiver penalty, and margin loss.
Both denote receiver-observed pre-FEC errors above the signal-degrade threshold while framing may remain.
Both denote polarization changing faster than the coherent receiver can track.
Both denote occurrence of monitored one-second intervals containing transmission errors.
Both denote insertion or onward carriage of ODU-AIS for affected downstream ODUs.
Both denote transmission of backward defect indication toward the far-end OTU source.
Both denote equipment ceasing to provide monitoring or telemetry.
Both describe unaffected comparison channels remaining in normal operation; A also allows the optical path generally.
Both denote internal detection of a fault in the current unit's transmit laser.
Both denote amplifier control that adjusts pump drive to maintain configured gain.
Both describe an upstream input-power reduction under gain control, including re-levelling, residual OSNR penalty, and low power for larger loss.
Both denote aggregate amplifier output below its expected level across carried channels.
Both denote a persistent downstream OSNR penalty, including after signal power is restored.
Both denote a unit or optical device having a dark output.
Both denote an input impairment traversing a transparent device without correction.
Both denote section-local containment of an OSC defect at the receiving node.
Both denote optical power remaining within its expected range despite another quality impairment.
Both denote increasing pump drive current to preserve configured amplifier gain.
Both denote an ageing trend eventually crossing the AMP_PUMP_EOL threshold.
Both denote below-normal optical power for a channel at a downstream observation point.
Both denote failure to receive the incoming optical supervisory channel on one section.
Both denote measured amplifier gain differing from target by more than 2 dB.
Both denote pump drive current exceeding 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
Both denote unavailability or interruption of the client-facing service.
Both denote a service configured with alternate working and protection ODU paths.
Both denote availability of at least one defect-free ODU path to the protection selector.
Both denote only a transient service interruption during protection switching.
Both denote a single ODU being switched to an unintended endpoint.
Both denote an ODU-layer misconnection with normal underlying optical indicators.
Both denote a line-wide ingress impairment continuing on each wavelength routed onward.
Both denote an impairment traversing a transparent node without being removed.
Both denote an optically present channel whose recoverable quality is degraded.
Both denote all channels on the affected WSS input being prevented from passing.
Both denote traffic outside the failed ingress or component continuing normally.
Both are measurements of optical power at the receive interface.
Both are client or transport errored-second counters reported in standard 15-minute intervals.
Both measure per-channel optical signal-to-noise ratio.
Both are the bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction.
Both measure differential group delay between polarization modes.
Both measure the temporal rate of state-of-polarization change.
Both measure aggregate optical power across all wavelengths at amplifier input.
Both measure aggregate optical power across all wavelengths at amplifier output.
Both measure pump drive current normalized to its beginning-of-life value.
Both indicate whether the incoming optical supervisory channel is detected.
Both are client unavailable-seconds performance counters.
Both provide a separate optical-power measurement for each wavelength.
Both denote the booster amplifier at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section.
Both denote an intermediate-site optical line amplifier.
Both denote the receive-side preamplifier at the end of a multiplex section.
Both denote an OTN device whose fabric cross-connects ODUs.
Both denote the generic client-facing service port class.
Both denote a colourless, directionless, contentionless ROADM routing wavelengths independently.
Both are the critical optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm.
Both are the critical OTU loss-of-frame alarm.
Both are the minor OTU signal-degrade alarm driven by excessive pre-FEC errors.
Both are the non-alarming OTU backward-defect indication.
Both are the critical transmit-laser equipment-failure alarm.
Both are the critical card-level equipment-failure alarm.
Both are critical amplifier input-loss alarms for absence of incoming traffic light.
Both are major alarms for absence of the incoming OSC on a fibre section.
Both are critical alarms indicating an amplifier has input light but no output.
Both indicate amplifier gain more than 2 dB from its target.
Both are minor pump end-of-life alarms based on normalized drive current.
Both are critical client service-failure alarms.
Both are non-alarming indications that ODU-AIS is being received.
Both are non-alarming ODU backward-defect indications.
Both are major ODU trail-trace mismatch alarms commonly revealing a misconnection.
Both indicate that the selector is carrying service on the protection path.
Both indicate that the standby protection ODU path is unavailable.
Both are critical client-port hardware-failure alarms.
Both are critical alarms for an internal OTN switch-fabric fault.
Both restrict impact to one optical wavelength channel.
Both denote traffic received and handled by the affected unit.
Both denote the affected unit's telemetry and status reporting.
Both denote the affected unit's derivative traffic alarms.
Both restrict the impairment to the particular receiver being diagnosed.
Both denote comparison channels outside the specifically affected channel or degree.
Both denote the end-to-end optical route traversed by the channel.
Both denote the complete set of channels carried by the affected aggregate, unit, or ingress degree.
Both denote a proper subset of channels, typically those at one spectral-band edge.
Both denote all relevant ODUs traversing the affected OTU or switch; B is specifically switch-scoped.
Both denote a single ODU trail or container.
Both denote the client-facing optical transceiver.
Both denote one affected interface or port, though A also explicitly includes a WSS input port.
Both denote the end-user traffic service carried through the network.
Both denote the remote receiver opposite the current transmitter.
Both denote the current local node or endpoint rather than the remote end.
Both denote the local optical line receiver where channel quality is assessed.
Both denote the remote transmitter feeding the current receiver.
Both locate a fault on the optical channel path, with A specifically restricting it to upstream points.
Both denote the currently managed equipment card.
Both denote points later in the traffic or signal direction.
Both denote the immediately upstream fibre section feeding the observing unit.
Both denote the nearest upstream optical amplifier.
Both denote ODU forwarding across the OTN switch fabric.
Both denote the ODU route currently selected to carry service traffic.
Both denote either endpoint of the client or ODU service.
Both denote an intermediate OTN switch traversed by the ODU.
Both denote a point on the primary working ODU route.
Both denote a point on the standby protection ODU route.
Both denote the specific currently managed interface port.
Both localize an OTN fabric defect to the current switch, with B naming its internal fabric more narrowly.
Both denote the entitlement or option required to expose optical power measurements.
Both denote the option required for advanced coherent and ageing measurements.
Both denote licensed channel-monitoring capability for per-wavelength power and related measurements.
Both denote an abrupt, definite, service-affecting functional failure.
Both denote partial performance degradation while signal or equipment remains operational.
Both denote gradual early deterioration detectable before hard failure.
Both denote the highest listed operational alarm severity.
Both denote the lower severity used for degradation, warning, or protection states.
Both denote a reported status or consequent indication that does not create an active alarm.
Both denote a serious alarm class below critical.
Both specify the G.798 actions of inserting ODU-AIS on every carried ODU and returning BDI after OTU frame loss.
Both describe independent per-wavelength ROADM switching; A additionally states how an ingress-wide impairment follows routed channels.
